walkthroughs.body_html:
Haiyan hit the Philippines on 8 Nov 2013.

• Winds: 315 km/h (one of strongest ever)
• 5m storm surge hit Tacloban
• ~6,300 deaths
• 14 million affected

An LIC response — heavily reliant on foreign aid.

Katrina hit New Orleans, USA on 29 Aug 2005.

• Cat 5 → Cat 3 at landfall
• Levees failed — 80% of city flooded
• ~1,800 deaths
• $125 billion damage

An HIC response — but slow and criticised.

Both storms revealed inequality:

• Haiyan: poor warning, weak buildings, slow aid
• Katrina: poorest areas worst hit, slow FEMA response
• Both spurred better preparation
• Both showed climate change risks

Vulnerability ≠ just hazard size.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.

mcqs.q: Why does the tropical rainforest have distinct vertical layers?
options: Rainforest layers exist because different animals live at different heights.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Competition for light: emergents (40m+), canopy (capturing most light), understorey (shade-tolerant) and forest floor (sparse vegetation due to low light) — each adapted to its light level.
Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.
